title: Building an AI assistant that makes phone calls [Convex Workshop]
talk_summary: A Convex DX engineer demos 'Floyd', a voice AI assistant that transcribes speech via Google STT, plans with GPT-4, and conducts phone calls through Twilio with real-time streaming, using Convex's reactive database to push state to clients without polling. The talk is mostly a product demo of Convex plus latency-tuning anecdotes; the transferable parts are the reactive-database-as-orchestration-bus pattern, pre-generated filler audio to mask cold-start latency, and prompt-size-driven latency growth.

takeaways.technique: Reactive DB as the agent work bus (no polling)
takeaways.what_they_do: Client writes a request row to the database; a server process holds a live subscription to 'pending' rows and picks work up automatically, writing status/transcript updates back that clients see for free.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's not polling we're not pinging the server to let it know it's got a reactive uh query that it's effectively subscribed to

takeaways.technique: Pre-generated filler to hide cold-start latency
takeaways.what_they_do: Because the first turn after pickup is slowest, they play a pre-recorded intro clip to buy time while the first LLM/TTS loop spins up.

takeaways.technique: Prompt size grows latency linearly; minimize every prompt
takeaways.what_they_do: They benchmark each pipeline stage and found that resending the full conversation each turn makes latency worsen as the call goes on; plan is to use threads and aggressively trim prompts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: as the conversation grows the prompt I'm sending to open AI that includes all of the previous conversation takes longer and longer

takeaways.technique: Pay for lower latency on the critical-path stage
takeaways.what_they_do: When TTS was the bottleneck (2-5s for a few sentences), the fix was to pay more for a lower-latency provider rather than tune parameters.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what I would do to fix that is I would pay more for lower latency or I would use another service

takeaways.what_they_do: When the agent lacks required info mid-task it says a canned 'I'll call you back', marks the request as missing something, and texts the user for the gap instead of hallucinating.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you're in a pickle and you just don't have the information that they're asking for you say I'm sorry I'm going to have to call you back

takeaways.technique: Two-phase plan-then-act with plan persisted as context
takeaways.what_they_do: Before acting, the model generates an action plan (extracted facts, steps) which is saved onto the request and fed back as context for the actual execution call.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the first thing I asked open AI to do is come up with an action plan ... I send this back in um as additional context when uh we're actually making the phone call
